name: rs_0001
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with two adjacent CN groups at the right-hand positions. Each of the two ring carbons next to them carries an OTos group, one at the top and one at the bottom. The two remaining ring carbons on the left are CH.

Tos is a tosyl group, 4-methylphenylsulfonyl: S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1. So each OTos is an O–S(=O)(=O)–C6H4–CH3 unit.

The ring is c1(OTos)c(C#N)c(C#N)c(OTos)cc1, which gives 3,6-bis(tosyloxy)phthalonitrile.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)Oc1ccc(OS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C)cc2)c(C#N)c1C#N

name: rs_0004
text:
The drawing shows 3-hydroxypyridine-2-carboxamide with an N-(2-methoxybenzyl) group.

**Pyridine ring:** The ring nitrogen is at the lower left. The carbon next to it (C2) carries the C(=O)NH group. The next carbon (C3) carries the OH.

**Amide and benzyl group:** The carbonyl carbon is bonded to NH, which is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to a benzene ring. The benzene carbon next to the CH2 attachment point carries OMe, so the methoxy group is ortho.

**SMILES:** Oc1cccnc1C(=O)NCc1ccccc1OC

Atom check: the pyridine ring has c1 (C–OH), c, c, c, n, c1 (C2), which is 6 atoms. The amide, CH2, and the benzene ring with OMe account for the rest.

SMILES: Oc1cccnc1C(=O)NCc1ccccc1OC

name: rs_0002
text:
The drawing shows an N-methylpiperazine whose second nitrogen carries a CH2 link to a benzene ring, and the ring bears an NO2 group.

**Piperazine ring:** There are two nitrogens. One carries a methyl group, shown as a line going to the left. The other connects through a CH2 to the aromatic ring.

**Aromatic ring:** The benzylic CH2 attaches at one ring carbon, the top-left vertex. Going clockwise, the next vertex is the top one, then the top-right vertex bearing NO2. The CH2 and NO2 are therefore separated by one carbon, which makes the substitution meta (3-nitrobenzyl).

**SMILES check:** CN1CCN(CC1)Cc1cccc(c1)[N+](=O)[O-] is valid. It has the methyl on N1, four ring CH2 groups, the benzyl CH2, and the nitro group meta to the CH2 attachment, matching the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)Cc1cccc(c1)[N+](=O)[O-]

name: rs_0003
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an oxindole (an eltrombopag-like scaffold).

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H and is attached at the meta position to the second ring. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon along carries the NH–N= group. So the second ring has the aryl group, OH and hydrazine on three consecutive carbons (positions 1, 2, 3).

**Oxindole part.** The ring system is an indol-2-one with the following substituents:
- C3 is double-bonded to N, forming the hydrazone.
- C2 is C=O.
- N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group.
- The fluorine sits on the benzo ring at C5, para to N1's attachment carbon C7a. In the drawing, C3a is the upper-left carbon of the benzo ring, C4 is the next carbon (top), C5 bears F, C6 follows, and C7 is bottom-right. F is on the upper-right carbon, which is C5.

**Hydrazone geometry.** The drawing gives no clear stereo specification, so I leave it out.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)
- Second ring: c2cccc(NN=C3...)c2O
- Oxindole: C3 = C(=O)N(Ar)c4ccc(F)cc34

Full SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(F)cc23)c1O

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(F)cc23)c1O

name: rs_0005
text:
The drawing shows a 4,5-dihydropyrazole (2-pyrazoline) ring, read region by region as follows.

- **Ring:** N1 carries the side chain, N2 is double-bonded to C3, C4 is a CH2, and C5 is a CH.
- **N1 substituent:** a CH2 attached to C(=O)OEt, which is an ethyl acetate group.
- **C5 substituent:** a 4-bromophenyl group.
- **C3 substituent:** a 4-methoxyphenyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** C5 is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

The SMILES, written from N1 around the ring, is CCOC(=O)CN1N=C(CC1c1ccc(Br)cc1)c1ccc(OC)cc1. Checking it atom for atom:

- N1 is bonded to the CH2 of the ester side chain.
- N1 is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C3 (the `C(...)` carrying the methoxyphenyl group).
- C3 is bonded to C4 (CH2), which is bonded to C5 (the `C1` carrying the bromophenyl group).
- C5 closes the ring back to N1.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)CN1N=C(CC1c1ccc(Br)cc1)c1ccc(OC)cc1

name: rs_0007
text:
The structure breaks into four parts.

**Left part.** An ethyl ester, EtO-C(=O)-CH2, is attached to N1 of a benzimidazol-2-one. N3 of the benzimidazolone carries a piperidin-4-yl group.

**Linker.** The piperidine N is bonded to CH2-CH(OH)-CH2, which connects to N1 of the pyrazole.

**Right part.** This is a 4,5,6,7-tetrahydro-pyrazolo[4,3-c]pyridine. The pyrazole N1 is bonded to C7a, which is bonded to C7 (CH2), then C6 (CH2), then N5 (bearing the SO2Me group), then C4 (CH2), then C3a. C3a is bonded to C3, which carries the 4-CF3-phenyl group, and C3 is bonded to N2. N2 is bonded to N1.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Ester and benzimidazolone: CCOC(=O)CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CC2)...)c2ccccc12
- Linker and pyrazole: CC(O)Cn1nc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)c2CN(S(C)(=O)=O)CCc12

The full SMILES is:

CCOC(=O)CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CC(O)Cn3nc(-c4ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc4)c4CN(S(C)(=O)=O)CCc34)CC2)c2ccccc12

The ring closures are consistent. In the pyrazole, n3 opens ring 3, then n, then c(aryl), then c4 (C3a, opens ring 4), then CN(...)CC, then c34 (C7a), which closes both rings 3 and 4. C7a bonds to n3 (N1) and to C3a (via ring 4), as required.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CC(O)Cn3nc(-c4ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc4)c4CN(S(C)(=O)=O)CCc34)CC2)c2ccccc12

name: rs_0010
text:
The image shows a benzene ring joined to a two-carbon alkene, which ends in a CHO group. This is cinnamaldehyde.

**Stereochemistry:** The ring attaches at about (260, 105) and the chain runs up to the first alkene carbon at (380, 35). It then goes down to the second alkene carbon at (510, 105) and up to CHO at (590, 60). The two substituents, the phenyl on the first carbon and the CHO on the second, lie on opposite sides of the double bond. Phenyl is attached to the first alkene carbon and leaves it toward the lower left. CHO leaves the second carbon toward the upper right. That is a zigzag arrangement, so the double bond is trans (E).

**SMILES:** Written with the stereo markers, the E form is O=C/C=C/c1ccccc1. Here "C/C=C/c" places the CHO carbon and the phenyl on opposite sides, which is trans, as drawn.

SMILES: O=C/C=C/c1ccccc1

name: rs_0009
text:
The drawing shows methyl (E)-3-(2,4-dinitrophenyl)acrylate.

**Ring.** The benzene ring has the vinyl chain attached at one carbon. An NO2 sits on the adjacent carbon (ortho, drawn at the bottom). A second O2N sits at the upper left, which is para to the chain carbon. So the nitro groups are at the 2 and 4 positions.

**Chain.** The ring carbon bears a CH=CH unit that leads to a C(=O)OCH3 group. The ester carbonyl oxygen is drawn at the bottom and the OMe at the upper right.

**Stereochemistry.** The ring carbon is at about (215, 105). The first alkene carbon is at about (275, 140) and the second at about (335, 105). The carbonyl carbon is at about (390, 140). The ring and the carbonyl carbon lie on opposite sides of the C=C bond, with the ring below-left and the carbonyl below-right of the alkene carbons. The first alkene carbon sits low and the second sits high, so the substituents point down on both ends, which would read as cis. Checking the geometry: the ring carbon (215, 105) connects to the first alkene carbon (275, 140), then to the second (335, 105), then to the carbonyl carbon (390, 140). This is a zigzag, with the ring carbon up, the first alkene carbon down, the second up, and the carbonyl down. A zigzag means the substituents are trans, so the alkene is E.

**SMILES.** Writing it with E geometry: COC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc(cc1[N+](=O)[O-])[N+](=O)[O-]

Check on the ring: c1 (attached to the chain), then c, c, c(NO2) at the para position, then c, then c1(NO2) at the ortho position. That is correct.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: rs_0008
text:
I read the molecule as a 4-substituted benzoic acid joined through a CH2CH2 linker to the nitrogen of a 2-pyrrolidinone (five-membered lactam).

- **Lactam ring:** N, C=O, two CH2 groups, and the C5 carbon, which carries the side chain.
- **Side chain on C5:** a trans CH=CH, then CH(OH), then three CH2 groups (counted from the zigzag), then CH(OH), then CH3.
- **Aryl part:** N–CH2CH2–C6H4–CO2H, para-substituted.

**Stereochemistry:**
- The ring carbon C5 has a wedge to the vinyl group, which gives `[C@H]` in the SMILES as written.
- The terminal carbinol carbon has a hashed OH, which gives `[C@H]` in the SMILES as written.
- The alkene is drawn trans (E).
- The allylic CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](/C=C/C(O)CCC[C@H](C)O)N1CCc1ccc(C(=O)O)cc1

name: rs_0011
text:
I read the molecule as a pyrrolidin-2-one ring with three attachments:

- **Ring nitrogen:** an N-CH2CH2 chain leading to a benzene ring that carries CO2H para to the chain.
- **C5 of the ring:** a trans CH=CH linker, drawn with a bold wedge on the bond from the ring carbon, which ends in a CH(OH) carbon.
- **The CH(OH) carbon:** it carries a hashed OH and is bonded to a CH2 that leads to a benzene ring with Cl meta to that CH2.

**Stereochemistry**
- Ring C5 has priorities N > vinyl carbon > ring CH2 > H. The wedge puts H at the back, and N → vinyl → CH2 runs clockwise, so this centre is R.
- The carbinol carbon has priorities OH > vinyl carbon > CH2 > H. The hashed OH puts H toward the viewer, and OH → vinyl → CH2 appears clockwise, which reverses to S.
- The double bond is drawn trans (E).

Writing the SMILES with the ring closure on the N side, C5 needs `@@` for R and the carbinol carbon needs `@@` for S.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(CCN2C(=O)CC[C@@H]2/C=C/[C@@H](O)Cc2cccc(Cl)c2)cc1

name: rs_0014
text:
The drawing shows a central benzene ring with three substituents, plus an amidinophenyl amide and a chloropyridyl amide.

**Central ring.** The OMe group sits at the top. Going around the ring, the carbon bearing the carboxamide C(=O)NH-pyridyl is adjacent to the carbon bearing the NH-C(=O)-aryl group. The OMe carbon is meta to the carboxamide carbon, which makes it para to the NH carbon.

Reading the ring vertices:
- Top: C–OMe.
- Upper right: CH, which connects down to the carbon bearing C(=O)NH.
- Lower right: C bearing the carboxamide.
- Bottom: C bearing the NH amide.
- Left, going back up: two CH carbons, ending at the top C–OMe.

So the carboxamide carbon (C1) is bonded to C2 (bearing NH) and C6 (CH). C6 is bonded to C5 (bearing OMe). The OMe is therefore para to the NH carbon, since C2 and C5 are para.

**Pyridine.** The ring is attached through its 2-position to the amide NH. The N is adjacent to C2, and Cl sits at the 5-position, which is para to C2.

**Amidinophenyl.** A para-substituted benzene carries C(=N)N at one end and C(=O)NH at the other.

**SMILES:** COc1ccc(NC(=O)c2ccc(C(=N)N)cc2)c(c1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1

SMILES: COc1ccc(NC(=O)c2ccc(C(=N)N)cc2)c(c1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1

name: rs_0006
text:
I read the drawing as a tetrahydropyran carrying four groups, and I assigned the stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes. Two chain lengths were hard to count in the image, so those are best guesses.

**Tetrahydropyran ring** (O1, then C2 to C6):
- C2 is the anomeric carbon. It carries a wedged OMe and the thiazolidinone C4 as a plain bond.
- C3 is a CH2.
- C4 carries the ester oxygen on a wedge.
- C5 is a CH2.
- C6 carries the alkenyl chain on a hash.

**Chain on C6:** I counted a but-3-enyl group (CH2CH2CH=CH2). The drawing could also be read as pent-4-enyl, so this is uncertain.

**Ester on C4:** I counted oct-7-enoate, C(=O) followed by five CH2 groups and CH=CH2. This could also be a shorter chain, so this count is uncertain too.

**Thiazolidin-2-one:**
- The ring is S1, C2(=O), N3, C4 and C5, with C5 a CH2.
- N3 carries a PMB group, which is CH2-C6H4-OMe with the OMe para.
- C4 carries a wedged H and is bonded to the pyran C2.

I derived each @/@@ label by working out the neighbour order around the centre in the SMILES. For C6 and the thiazolidinone C4 the implicit H sits at the front or back, and for C2 the wedged OMe is the front substituent.

SMILES: C=CCC[C@@H]1C[C@@H](OC(=O)CCCCCC=C)C[C@@](OC)(O1)[C@@H]2CSC(=O)N2Cc3ccc(OC)cc3

name: rs_0012
text:
I read the molecule as a 9-membered dilactone core with the substituents below.

**Substituents**
- The pyridine has a 4-OMe group.
- It has a 3-O-C(=O)-O-CH2-C≡C-CH3 carbonate (but-2-ynyl carbonate).
- At C2 it carries a C(=O)NH amide.

**Dilactone ring (9 atoms)**
- The ring runs: CH(NH-amide) – C(=O) – O – CH(CH3) – CH(O-isobutyryl) – CH(CH2Ph) – C(=O) – O – CH2, closing back on the first CH.

**Stereocentres**
Assigned from the wedges and hashes, each checked against the SMILES atom order:

| Centre | Substituent drawn | CIP | SMILES tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| CH–N | hashed N | S | `@` |
| CH–Bn | wedged benzyl | R | `@` |
| CH–O-isobutyryl | hashed O | R | `@@` |
| CH–CH3 | wedged methyl | S | `@` |

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H]2COC(=O)[C@H](Cc3ccccc3)[C@@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@H](C)OC2=O)c1OC(=O)OCC#CC

name: rs_0017
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with an OH group at the top and a COOH group at the bottom. These are para to each other, so the molecule is 4-hydroxybenzoic acid.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: rs_0015
text:
The drawing shows a coumarin (2H-chromen-2-one) core with these substituents:

- C2 is the lactone carbonyl (C=O), and O1 is the ring oxygen.
- C3 carries a CH2C(=O)NH-aryl group.
- C4 carries a 3-formylphenyl group.
- C6 carries a methyl group and C7 carries a chlorine. In the drawing, the Cl-bearing carbon is the top-left vertex and the methyl-bearing carbon is the next one down. Going around the benzo ring, C8 is the CH adjacent to the carbon bonded to O (C8a), C7 bears Cl, C6 bears CH3, and C5 is the CH.
- The anilide aryl ring is attached at N. Its ortho position carries CF3 and its para position carries Cl, giving 4-chloro-2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl.

SMILES for the coumarin: O=C1Oc2cc(Cl)c(C)cc2C(c2cccc(C=O)c2)=C1CC(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cc1C(F)(F)F

Atom check on the benzo ring: c2 (C8a), then cc(Cl) is C8 and C7(Cl), then c(C) is C6, then c is C5, and c2 is C4a, which is followed by C4. This matches the drawing.

Aniline ring: N–c1 (C1), c (C6, H), c (C5, H), c(Cl) (C4), c (C3, H), c1 (C2) with CF3. The ring is written as c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(F)(F)F, so C1 is bonded to N, then C6 and C5 are CH, C4 bears Cl, C3 is CH, and C2 bears CF3. This is correct.

SMILES: O=C1Oc2cc(Cl)c(C)cc2C(c2cccc(C=O)c2)=C1CC(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cc1C(F)(F)F

name: rs_0018
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary carbon carrying four groups: a phenyl (Ph), a hydroxyl (OH), an ethynyl group (the triple bond running to the right), and a 2-hydroxyphenyl ring.

The hydroxyphenyl ring is attached to the quaternary carbon at one position, and its neighbouring ring carbon bears OH (shown at the bottom). The OH is therefore ortho to the attachment point.

The quaternary carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but all its bonds are drawn plain, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: C#CC(O)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1O

name: rs_0013
text:
I read the molecule as a nine-membered dilactone ring carrying four stereocentres, joined through an amide to a 4-methoxypyridine whose 3-oxygen is esterified by a 3-(2,6-dichlorophenyl)-5-methylisoxazole-4-carbonyl group.

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring runs: C(=O), O, CH(CH3), CH(O-isobutyryl), CH(CH2Ph), C(=O), O, CH2, CH(NH-). The CH(NH-) carbon closes back to the first C(=O).
- The amide nitrogen on the CH(NH-) carbon is acylated by the pyridine-2-carbonyl group.
- The pyridine has OMe at C4 and the ester oxygen at C3.
- The isoxazole is O1, N2, C3 (2,6-dichlorophenyl), C4 (carbonyl), C5 (methyl).

**Stereochemistry** (assigned from the drawn wedges and hashes)
- The CH bearing N has a hashed N bond, giving `[C@H]`.
- The CH bearing CH3 has a wedged methyl, giving `[C@H]`.
- The CH bearing the isobutyrate oxygen has a hashed O bond, giving `[C@@H]`.
- The CH bearing the benzyl group has a wedged benzyl, giving `[C@H]`.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H]2COC(=O)[C@H](Cc3ccccc3)[C@@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@H](C)OC2=O)c1OC(=O)c1c(C)onc1-c1c(Cl)cccc1Cl

name: rs_0019
text:
The structure is a xanthone joined to a chromone (flavone-type) unit, so I read it as two ring systems and then connected them.

**Xanthone part**
- The left ring of the xanthone carries, from the top: an acetyl group (C(=O)Me) next to the ring oxygen, a methyl group, and the bond to the chromone.
- Going around this ring: C4 bears the acetyl, C3 bears the methyl, C2 bears the chromone, C1 is the CH, then C9a, C9 (the C=O), and C4a, which is bonded to the ring O.
- The right ring carries a COOH, two OH groups and a CH. Starting at the carbon next to C9 (C8a): C8 has COOH, C7 has OH, C6 has OH, C5 is CH, and C4b is bonded to the O.

**Chromone part**
- C2 is attached to the xanthone and to the ring O1.
- C3 is a CH and C4 is the C=O.
- C4a is the fusion carbon next to C4, and C5 bears COOMe.
- C6 is a CH, C7 bears OH, C8 is a CH, and C8a is bonded to O1.

**SMILES assembly**
- Left xanthone ring: c1(C(C)=O) c(C) c(–chromone) c c2 c1 O c3 c c(O) c(O) c(C(=O)O) c3 C2=O.
- Written out: CC(=O)c1c(C)c(cc2c1Oc1cc(O)c(O)c(C(=O)O)c1C2=O)-c1cc(=O)c2c(C(=O)OC)cc(O)cc2o1.

Ring closures check out: in the xanthone, ring 1 opens at the acetyl-bearing carbon and closes at c1 (C4a) after "c2c1". In "c2c1Oc1cc(O)c(O)c(C(=O)O)c1C2=O", the label 2 opens at C9a and closes at C9 (C2=O). The new ring label 1 is reused for the right ring, which is allowed because the first ring 1 has already closed. In the chromone, c1cc(=O)c2c(C(=O)OC)cc(O)cc2o1 closes properly.

SMILES: CC(=O)c1c(C)c(cc2c1Oc1cc(O)c(O)c(C(=O)O)c1C2=O)-c1cc(=O)c2c(C(=O)OC)cc(O)cc2o1

name: rs_0016
text:
I read the molecule as three parts and wrote the SMILES from them.

**Left fragment:** an indane (2,3-dihydro-1H-indene) carrying a carboxylic acid on the five-membered ring at C2. The aromatic carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon (position 4) carries the sulfonyl group.

**Central ring:** a piperazine. N1 bears the indane sulfonyl group and N4 bears the aryl sulfonyl group. The carbons next to N1 (C2 and C6) each carry a methyl, and both methyls are drawn as wedges, so the two methyls are cis.

**Right fragment:** a 4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl ring attached to N4 through a sulfonyl group.

**Stereochemistry:** with the implicit hydrogen pointing away from the viewer, the top stereocentre reads Me → CH2 → N clockwise, which gives `[C@@H]` in the order I wrote it. The bottom stereocentre reads N → CH2 → Me clockwise, which gives `[C@H]`. The C2 of the indane is not drawn with a wedge, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1Cc2cccc(c2C1)S(=O)(=O)N1[C@@H](C)CN(S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc2)C[C@H]1C

name: rs_0020
text:
This structure is tamsulosin. I read it region by region.

- **Right side:** a 2-ethoxyphenoxy group (benzene ring with adjacent OEt and O–CH2CH2) is attached through the O–CH2CH2 chain to an NH.
- **Centre:** the NH is bonded to a stereocentre carrying a methyl group and a CH2 that leads to the other aromatic ring.
- **Left ring:** a benzene ring bears the CH2 substituent, an OMe group para to it, and an SO2NH2 group ortho to the OMe.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is on a hashed bond, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CH2Ar > CH3 > H. In the drawing, N (upper right) → CH2 (upper left) → CH3 (down) runs counterclockwise. Because the H faces the viewer, this reverses to clockwise, which gives the R configuration. The SMILES below was checked to encode R.

SMILES: CCOc1ccccc1OCCN[C@H](C)Cc1ccc(OC)c(c1)S(N)(=O)=O

name: rs_0021
text:
The drawing shows a cyclohexene ring with a CF3 group on one carbon and a triflate (OSO2CF3) on a vinyl carbon.

Ring: the carbon bearing the CF3 is at the top left. Going around, the ring has a CH2 at the top right, then the C(OTf) carbon at the right. A C=C double bond runs from that carbon to the bottom CH, followed by a CH2 at the lower left, which closes back to the CF3 carbon.

So the ring is C1(OTf)=CCC(CF3)CC1. The C=C sits between the C–O carbon and the CH at the bottom. The CF3 carbon is separated from the C–O carbon by CH2 on the top path (two bonds) and by CH2–CH= on the bottom path (three bonds), which makes it the 4-position of a cyclohex-1-enyl triflate.

The CF3-bearing carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

The triflate is O–S(=O)(=O)–CF3.

SMILES: O=S(=O)(OC1=CCC(C(F)(F)F)CC1)C(F)(F)F

name: rs_0022
text:
The drawing shows three parts joined in a row: a substituted pyridine, an amide to a para-disubstituted benzene, and an ether to a substituted pyrimidine.

**Pyridine ring.** The ring nitrogen is at the bottom left. Going around the ring, the carbon next to N bears the C(=O)NH group (C2). The next carbon bears OH (C3), and the next bears OMe (C4). The remaining two ring carbons are unsubstituted.

**Amide and benzene.** The C2 carbon carries C(=O)N–H, and that nitrogen is bonded to a benzene ring. The ring is para-substituted, with an O at the opposite end.

**Pyrimidine.** The ether oxygen links the benzene to a pyrimidine carbon. That carbon is C4 of the pyrimidine, with N3 beside it. The other nitrogen, N1, sits on the far side of C2–H. C6 carries OPh, and C5 is CH.

**SMILES:** The pyridine part is `COc1ccnc(C(=O)N...)c1O`. The amide nitrogen leads to `c2ccc(cc2)Oc3cc(Oc4ccccc4)ncn3`.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(Oc3cc(Oc4ccccc4)ncn3)cc2)c1O

name: rs_0026
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Furan:** a furan-2-carboxylic acid with a CH2 substituent at C5. The ring is O1, C2 (COOH), C3, C4, C5 (CH2).

name: rs_0031
text:
I read the structure in three parts: the biphenyl acid, the hydrazone linker, and the N-aryl oxindole.

**Biphenyl acid (top left).** The ring carrying HO2C has a methyl on the carbon next to the carboxyl-bearing carbon. The ring runs from C1 (bearing CO2H) to C2 (bearing CH3), then C3, which is attached to the second aryl ring. Going around: C1(COOH), C2(CH3), C3(H), C4(aryl), C5(H), C6(H). This gives the 3-methyl-4-carboxyphenyl pattern, so the SMILES fragment is OC(=O)c1ccc(cc1C)-Ar.

**Middle ring.** It is attached to the acid ring at one carbon. The adjacent carbon bears OH, and the next carbon bears NH–N=. Ring: c1(Ar)c(O)c(NN=...)ccc1.

**Oxindole.** C3 is the hydrazone carbon (C=N), C2 is the carbonyl, and N1 carries the 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The benzo ring carries CF3. C3a is bonded to C4, which is the top carbon. Going around the benzo ring: C3a, C4 (top), C5 (right top), C6 (CF3, right bottom), C7 (bottom), C7a (bonded to N). So CF3 sits at position 6, matching the drawing.

**Oxindole SMILES.** C3(=NN...)C(=O)N(Ar)c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc23. Here c2 is C7a, then c is C7, then c(CF3) is C6, then cc are C5 and C4, and c23 is C3a. This is consistent.

**N-aryl group.** The 3,4-dimethylphenyl ring is attached at C1, with methyls at C3 and C4: c1ccc(C)c(C)c1.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn with a defined geometry. NH is on N, and N is double-bonded to C3. At C3 the substituents are C2 (carbonyl, lower left) and C3a (right). The N lies above-left of C3, and the NH lies to the left of N and slightly above it. I'll assign the geometry from coordinates. HN is at (350,372), N at (418,385), C3 at (447,440), C2 at (415,500), and C3a at (515,462). On the N side, HN lies to the upper left of the N=C axis. On the C3 side, the axis runs from N (418,385) down to C3 (447,440), so the direction is down and to the right. HN at (350,372) lies to the left of this axis. C2 at (415,500) is relative to C3 at (447,440), and the cross product shows it also lies to the left, so HN and C2 are on the same side (Z relationship with the carbonyl).

Writing the SMILES as N/N=C3/C(=O)...: with the NH written before the N, the fragment is c(N/N=C3\C(=O)N...), where "/" and "\" encode the cis relationship between NH and C(=O). In F/C=C\F the two F atoms are cis, so N/N=C\C(=O) places NH and C2 cis. I use that form.

SMILES: Cc1cc(ccc1C(=O)O)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc23)c1O

I wrote the final SMILES with "/C2/" rather than "\C2", so I need to check that it is consistent. In "N/N=C2/C(=O)", the bond before N is "/" (N is above... ), and the bond after C2 is "/", which gives F/C=C/F, the trans form. That would put NH trans to C2, contradicting the cis assignment. The correct string uses "\" after C2:

SMILES: Cc1cc(ccc1C(=O)O)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc23)c1O

name: rs_0049
text:
The drawing is a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin core.

**Biphenyl part.** The top-left ring carries CO2H and is attached at the meta position to the second ring. In the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the C–OH carbon, which is adjacent to the C–NH carbon. So the NH sits ortho to OH, and OH sits ortho to the biaryl bond. This is a 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl-biphenyl-3'-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone linker.** The NH–N= unit connects to C3 of the indolinone, with the double bond to C3.

**Indolinone part.** C3 is bonded to C3a. C2 is the C=O and N1 carries the aryl group. The benzo ring runs C3a, C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a. The drawing places F on C4 (next to C3a) and F on C5. The N-aryl group is 3,4-dimethylphenyl.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. NH sits on the lower-left of N, and from C3 the C=O side points down-left while the C4 side points right. The hydrazone N is up-left of C3, and its NH goes to the left and down. Take the coordinates as C3 (~335, 460), N (~295, 400), NH (~230, 380).

- At C3, the substituents are C2 (down-left, at ~295, 510) and C3a (right, at ~440, 430).
- At N, the substituent is NH at (230, 380), to the left of N and slightly lower.
- The N=C bond runs from (295, 400) to (335, 460), going down-right.
- NH is on the left of this bond. C2 (295, 510) is also on the left or below it. So NH and C2 lie on the same side, which makes NH cis to C2(=O) and gives the Z isomer.

Writing the SMILES with this geometry: `N(/N=C1/C(=O)N(...)c2ccc(F)c(F)c12)` needs checking. With the fragment written as `c1...N/N=C2\C(=O)...`, I will use the pattern `Nc...` → `N/N=C1/C(=O)...`. In `X/N=C/Y`, X and Y are on opposite sides. Written as `N(aryl)/N=C1\C(=O)N...`, the aryl-N and C(=O) are on the same side, which is Z. I use the backslash form for the same-side arrangement.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(F)c(F)c23)c1O

Checking the stereo in this string: `N/N=C2/C(=O)` places the aryl-N and C(=O) on opposite sides (E). To get the Z form I want, I change it to the backslash form.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(F)c(F)c23)c1O

name: rs_0056
text:
This is a spiro fluoran dye: a xanthene core spiro-fused to a phthalide (isobenzofuranone).

**Left ring.** It carries the N(Et)(isopentyl) group. The isopentyl chain is N–CH2–CH2–CH(CH3)2, with the branch at the third carbon, which matches the drawing.

**Right ring.** It carries a methyl group and an NHPh group. Going around the ring from the oxygen-bearing carbon, the next carbon is CH, then C(Me), then C(NHPh), then CH, then the carbon attached to the spiro carbon. So Me sits next to the CH adjacent to C–O, and NHPh sits next to the CH adjacent to the spiro-bound carbon.

**Spiro carbon.** It bonds to the left ring, the right ring, the lactone oxygen, and the benzo ring. The lactone is O–C(=O)–aryl.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Spiro carbon with the lactone: C1(OC(=O)c2ccccc12)
- Left ring: c3ccc(N(CC)CCC(C)C)cc3O…, where the ring closure connects the carbon bearing O to the right ring.
- Right ring: c4cc(Nc5ccccc5)c(C)cc4 closes back to O. Written from the spiro-bound carbon, the right ring is c4cc(NPh)c(C)cc4O.

Full SMILES: CCN(CCC(C)C)c1ccc2c(c1)Oc1cc(C)c(Nc3ccccc3)cc1C21OC(=O)c2ccccc21

**Check of the ring closures.**
- Left ring: c1ccc2c(c1)O… The N-bearing carbon is c1. Then c, c, then c2, which is the spiro-attached carbon, then c(c1), which is the carbon bearing O. This gives N-carbon, CH, CH, C(spiro-side), C–O, CH back to N-carbon, so N is meta to O. That is correct.
- Right ring: Oc1cc(C)c(Nc3ccccc3)cc1C2… The O-bearing carbon is c1, then CH, then C(Me), then C(NHPh), then CH, then c1 (spiro-attached). Me is adjacent to the CH next to C–O, and NHPh is adjacent to the CH next to the spiro-attached carbon. This matches the drawing.
- Spiro carbon: C21 closes ring 2 to the left ring's c2 and opens a new ring 1 for the lactone, ending in c2ccccc21. The label 2 is reused after it closes. In "C21OC(=O)c2ccccc21", the spiro atom closes ring 2 and opens ring 1. Then c2 opens a new ring 2 and the final c21 closes both ring 2 (benzo) and ring 1 (spiro). This is valid.

SMILES: CCN(CCC(C)C)c1ccc2c(c1)Oc1cc(C)c(Nc3ccccc3)cc1C21OC(=O)c2ccccc21

text:
The structure breaks down into three regions.

**Left region.** A thiomorpholine ring (S at the far left, N at the right) is attached through the nitrogen to a carbon bearing =NH, forming an amidine: N1CCSCC1 with C(=N). That amidine carbon is bonded to a benzene ring. On that ring, the carbon bearing the C(=O)NH group sits para to the amidine. - **Indazole:** the carbonyl is on the benzo ring carbon next to C7, which makes it indazole-6-carbonyl. The ring has a free N–H.
- **Tetrahydroisoquinoline:** the indazole acyl group sits on N2. The aromatic ring carries Cl at C5 and C7, and the C6 carboxamide lies between them.
- **Side chain:** the amide NH leads to a CH bearing CO2H, then CH2–NH. That NH is attached to C(=N–C≡N), which is bonded to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** it carries OH groups at C3 (bold wedge) and C4 (hashed bond).

**Stereochemistry (CIP)**
- **α-Carbon:** the CH2 is on a wedge, and the priorities are N > CO2H > CH2N > H. Viewed with H at the back, N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This corresponds to `N[C@@H](CN…)C(=O)O` in the SMILES.
- **Piperidine C3:** the OH is on the wedge, with priorities OH > C4 > C2 > H. This gives S, written `[C@H]` in the SMILES.
- **Piperidine C4:** the OH is hashed, so H faces the viewer. The priorities are OH > C3 > C5 > H, and the reversed reading gives S, written `[C@@H]` in the SMILES.

That makes five sulfur atoms in a chain, S–S–S–S–S, with the two ends attached to the benzene carbons. The ring is therefore 2 carbons plus 5 sulfurs = 7 members.

The benzene ring has two OMe groups. The top-right carbon bears S, and the carbon to its left bears OMe (top). The next carbon to the left bears the second OMe. The two remaining carbons at the bottom are CH, and the bottom-right carbon bears S.

Writing the SMILES by walking around the benzene ring:
- c1 (bearing S, top right of the ring), attached to S1.
- c2 (bearing OMe, top).
- c3 (bearing OMe, left).
- c4 (CH) and c5 (CH).
- c6 (bearing S, bottom right), closing the ring.

Checking this string: c1 (OMe) is followed by c(OC), which is the second OMe carbon. Next comes c2, which carries the sulfur chain, then SSSSS, then c2, which closes the seven-membered ring. Then cc1 gives the two CH carbons and closes the benzene ring. The benzene ring is c1, c(OC), c2, c2', c, c, which is 6 atoms. text:

**Pyridine part.** The aromatic ring is a pyridine. Its C2 carries the amide carbonyl, C3 carries the O–C(=O)CH2CH2OMe ester, and C4 carries OMe.

**Nine-membered ring.** Going around the ring I get nine atoms:
1. lactone C=O
2. ring O
3. CH(CH3), methyl on a wedge
4. CH–O-acyl, hashed
5. CH(CH2Ph), benzyl on a wedge
6. lactone C=O
7. ring O
8. CH2
9. CH–NH, hashed

The second acyl group, on the ring oxygen at position 4, is another C(=O)CH2CH2OMe.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned the four ring stereocentres from the wedges and hashes:
- CH–N: `[C@H]`
- CH(Bn): `[C@H]`
- CH–O-acyl: `[C@@H]`
- CH(CH3): `[C@H]`

The SMILES is written to match this connectivity, and the ring-closure digits are paired.

SMILES: COCCC(=O)Oc1c(OC)ccnc1C(=O)N[C@H]2COC(=O)[C@H](Cc3ccccc3)[C@@H](OC(=O)CCOC)[C@H](C)OC2=O

name: rs_0106
text:
The drawing shows a 2-methyl-2-phenoxypropanoic acid unit, so I read it region by region.

- **Acid end:** HOOC–C(CH3)2–O–, where the oxygen is bonded to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Linker:** the para position of the benzene carries a CH2CH2 chain that ends at a nitrogen.
- **Nitrogen substituents:** the nitrogen carries a 5-ethylpyrimidin-2-yl group and a 2-cyanobenzyl group (CH2 on a benzene ring that bears an ortho C≡N).
- **Pyrimidine:** the ring has N at positions 1 and 3. C2 is attached to the amine nitrogen, and C5 bears the ethyl group.

Writing the pyrimidine as c1ncc(CC)cn1 puts C2 between the two ring nitrogens and C5 opposite it, which matches the drawing.

The SMILES is OC(=O)C(C)(C)Oc1ccc(CCN(Cc2ccccc2C#N)c2ncc(CC)cn2)cc1. It contains no stereocentres, and the drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry, so none is encoded.

SMILES: CCc1cnc(nc1)N(CCc1ccc(OC(C)(C)C(=O)O)cc1)Cc1ccccc1C#N

This makes the molecule 3,6-bis(p-tolylthio)phthalonitrile.

name: rs_0109
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Pyridine ring:** N at the left, with Cl at the 3 and 5 positions and the 4-position bearing O. This is a 3,5-dichloropyridin-4-yl ether.
- **Piperidine:** the 4-position carries the ether O, and the ring N is attached to the chain CH2–CH(OH)–CH2.
- **Pyrazole:** the chain CH2 is bonded to N1 of the pyrazole. N1 is bonded to N2, which is double-bonded to C3, and C3 bears the 4-CF3-phenyl group. C3 is bonded to C3a, which is double-bonded to C7a, and C7a is bonded to N1.
- **Fused tetrahydropyridine ring:** C3a–CH2–N(Ac)–CH2–CH2–C7a. The N carries an acetyl group, C(=O)CH3.

SMILES assembly:
- Pyridine and ether: Clc1cncc(Cl)c1OC2CCN(CC2)...
- Chain: CC(O)Cn3nc(c4ccc(cc4)C(F)(F)F)c5CN(C(C)=O)CCc35

The CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

Full SMILES: Clc1cncc(Cl)c1OC1CCN(CC1)CC(O)Cn1nc(-c2ccc(cc2)C(F)(F)F)c2CN(C(C)=O)CCc12

Ring-closure check: ring 1 is reused after the pyridine closes, which is valid. In the pyrazole, n1 opens ring 1, c2 opens the phenyl ring and closes it, then c2 opens the fused ring, and c12 at the end closes both ring 1 and ring 2. The last atom c12 is C7a, bonded to n1 and to c2 (C3a), which is correct.

SMILES: Clc1cncc(Cl)c1OC1CCN(CC1)CC(O)Cn1nc(-c2ccc(cc2)C(F)(F)F)c2CN(C(C)=O)CCc12

name: rs_0110
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

**Left bicyclic part.** The benzene-type ring is drawn with only one double bond in its upper half, and its lower-left part has CH2–CH2 or CH2–CH(N) saturation. Going around the ring:
- The top-right carbon is C4a, joined to C4, which carries the methyl.
- Going left from C4a, the top-left carbon is a CH that is double-bonded to C4a.
- Next is a CH2 at the far left top, then a CH bearing N(Et)2 at the lower left.
- Then comes C8 (CH) double-bonded to C8a, which is attached to the ring O.

The drawing shows a double bond at the top between C5 and C4a (the "=" inside the ring top), and another double bond between C8 and C8a at the bottom. The C6 position is CH2 and C7 is CH(NEt2).

**Pyran ring.** It contains C4a, C4(CH3)=C3, C2 (exocyclic double bond to the barbiturate carbon), O1, and C8a.

**Right part.** This is a thiobarbiturate: C5 (=C2 of the pyran), C4(=O), N(Bu), C(=S), N(Bu), C6(=O).

**SMILES construction:**
- Start with the barbiturate: O=C1N(CCCC)C(=S)N(CCCC)C(=O)C1=C2...
- The pyran ring is C2 (=C1 exocyclic), then C=C(C)C3=CCC(N(CC)CC)C=C3O2.
- Checking ring closure: C2 is attached to O and to C3H. C3H=C4(CH3), then C4–C4a. C4a=C5H, C5H–C6H2, C6H2–C7H(NEt2), C7H–C8H=C8a, and C8a is bonded to C4a and to O.
- So the pyran ring is C2(=C...)–C3H=C4(C)–C4a(=C5)–C8a(=C8)–O1.

Full SMILES: CCCCN1C(=O)C(=C2C=C(C)C3=CCC(N(CC)CC)C=C3O2)C(=O)N(CCCC)C1=S

Checking C4a: it has a bond to C4, a double bond to C5, and a bond to C8a, which makes 4 valences. C8a has a bond to C4a, a double bond to C8, and a bond to O, which also makes 4. This matches the SMILES, where C3 is the ring-opening atom "C3=CCC(...)C=C3O2".

SMILES: CCCCN1C(=O)C(=C2C=C(C)C3=CCC(N(CC)CC)C=C3O2)C(=O)N(CCCC)C1=S

name: rs_0111
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

**Left fragment.** This is an imidazo[4,5-b]pyridin-2-one. N1 carries a methyl group and is attached to the carbonyl carbon C2 (C=O). N3 carries the piperidin-4-yl group and is bonded to C3a, which is also bonded to the pyridine N. The pyridine ring runs C3a, N4, C5(OMe), C6, C7, C7a, and C7a is bonded to N1.

SMILES for this fragment: CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CC2)...)c2nc(OC)ccc12

**Middle linker.** The piperidine N is bonded to CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2, then the pyrazole N1.

**Right fragment.** This is a 4,5,6,7-tetrahydro-pyrazolo[4,3-c]pyridine.
- The pyrazole N1 is bonded to C7a, and N1 is also bonded to N2.
- N2 double-bonds to C3, which carries the 4-CF3-phenyl group.
- C3 is bonded to C3a, and C3a=C7a.
- C3a is bonded to C4 (CH2), which is bonded to N5 (bearing SO2Me).
- N5 is bonded to C6 (CH2), then C7 (CH2), then C7a.

SMILES for this fragment: n1(CC(O)CN...)nc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)c2c1CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C2

**Full SMILES:**
CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CC2)CC(O)Cn2nc(-c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3)c3c2CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C3)c2nc(OC)ccc12

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo label.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CC2)CC(O)Cn2nc(-c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3)c3c2CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C3)c2nc(OC)ccc12

name: rs_0105
text:
I read the molecule as a 9-membered dilactone core carrying four substituents.

**Core ring (9 atoms):** C(=O)–O–CH(CH3)–CH(O-isobutyrate)–CH(CH2Ph)–C(=O)–O–CH2–CH(NH–), closing back to the first C(=O).

**Substituents:**
- The ring CH bearing the amide NH carries a picolinamide: the NH is acylated by a pyridine-2-carbonyl group.
- That pyridine has a 4-OMe group and, at position 3, an ester O–C(=O) to a 4-methyl-1,2,3-thiadiazol-5-yl ring.
- The O-acyl group on the ring is isobutyrate, OC(=O)CH(CH3)2.
- The ring CH next to the lactone carbonyl carries a benzyl group, CH2Ph.
- The ring CH bonded to the ring oxygen carries a methyl group, shown as a wedge.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned the four ring stereocentres from the drawing:
- The NH is on a hashed bond.
- The benzyl is on a wedge.
- The isobutyrate O is on a hashed bond.
- The methyl is on a wedge.

I converted each to @/@@ by working out the neighbour order in the SMILES. I did this by hand, so the stereo marks are the part most open to error.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H]2COC(=O)[C@H](Cc3ccccc3)[C@@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@H](C)OC2=O)c1OC(=O)c1snnc1C

text:

text:

name: rs_0114
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Benzofuran:** a benzene ring fused to a furan. The furan oxygen sits at the bottom, C2 carries an n-butyl chain (four carbons), and C3 carries a CH2 linker.
- **Biphenyl core:** the CH2 attaches to a para-disubstituted phenyl ring, which connects directly to a second phenyl ring.

In the drawing, the ring carbon at the lower left of the ring (the one bonded to the first phenyl) is attached to a CH, then to the NH-bearing carbon, then to the O-bearing carbon, then to a CH, then to another CH, and back to the start. So the O and N groups are ortho to each other, and the N-bearing carbon is meta to the biphenyl link.

name: rs_0107
text:
I read the structure as three parts joined by amide bonds, then assigned the two stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Pyridine part:** The ring is a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypyridine with a carboxamide at C2, next to the ring nitrogen. That gives `COc1ccnc(C(=O)N...)c1O`.

**Cyclohexane core:** Going around the ring from the carbon that carries the NH:
- CH(NH) with a bold wedge to N
- CH2
- a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl and a C(=O)N(CH3)CH2CH2Ph group, drawn with a hashed bond
- CH2
- C(CH3)2
- CH2, closing back to the CH(NH)

**Side chain:** The amide is N-methyl-N-(2-phenylethyl), written `C(=O)N(C)CCc3ccccc3`.

**Stereochemistry:**
- For the CH(NH) carbon, the wedge puts N toward the viewer and H behind. The priorities are N, then the CH2 leading to the quaternary carbon, then the other CH2. This gives R, which is `[C@H]` in the SMILES order I wrote.
- For the quaternary carbon, the hashed C(=O)N is behind the plane. The priorities are C(=O)N, then the CH2 toward the CH(NH) carbon, then the CH2 toward the CMe2 carbon, then CH3. Converting this to SMILES neighbour order gives `[C@]`.

The SMILES below is written to match the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H]2C[C@](C)(C(=O)N(C)CCc3ccccc3)CC(C)(C)C2)c1O

name: rs_0116
text:
The drawing is a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H and is attached at the meta position to the second ring. In the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon along bears the NH–N= group. So the substituents run biaryl, OH, NH in consecutive positions, which makes the ring 3'-hydrazinyl-2'-hydroxybiphenyl-3-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone and isatin.** The NH is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C3 of the indol-2-one. C2 is the C=O, and the ring nitrogen N1 carries an aryl group.

**N-aryl group.** The ring is attached to N at C1. Going around it, the CF3 sits at a meta position (C3) and the methyl at C4, so it is 4-methyl-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(c4)C(F)(F)F)c5ccccc35)c2O
- Check on the second ring: c2 (attached to the acid ring), then c, c, c, then c(NN...) and c2O. The OH carbon closes the ring and is adjacent to both the biaryl carbon and the NH carbon, as required.
- The C=N geometry is not clearly specified in the drawing, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(c4)C(F)(F)F)c5ccccc35)c2O

text:

name: rs_0120
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents.

- A nitrile (C≡N) is attached at the upper right ring carbon.

- The nitro group (O2N) is attached at the upper left ring carbon.

To place the nitro group, number the ring with the nitrile carbon as C1 and the fluorine carbon as C2. Going the other way from C1, the next carbon is the top vertex (C6), and the nitro-bearing carbon is the one after it (C5). The nitro group is therefore para to the fluorine and meta to the nitrile, which gives 2-fluoro-5-nitrobenzonitrile.

name: rs_0115
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-pyrrolidinone whose ring nitrogen carries a –CH2CH2– link to the 5-position of a thiophene-2-carboxylic acid.

- **Lactam ring:** the five-membered ring has a C=O next to N, then two CH2 groups, then a CH at the ring carbon beside N.
- **N-substituent:** N–CH2–CH2– is attached to thiophene C5. The thiophene S is flanked by C2 (bearing CO2H) and C5.
- **Side chain on the ring CH:** a trans (E) CH=CH leads to a CH(OH) carbon, which carries an n-pentyl chain (five carbons).
- **Stereochemistry:** the carbinol carbon is drawn with a hashed bond to OH, so OH points away from the viewer and H points toward the viewer. The priorities are OH > vinyl > pentyl > H. OH, vinyl and pentyl run clockwise as drawn, and because H faces the viewer the true configuration is reversed, giving S. In the SMILES this corresponds to `[C@@H]`.
- **Unspecified centre:** the ring CH is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(CCN2C(=O)CCC2/C=C/[C@@H](O)CCCCC)s1

name: rs_0122
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

**Left bicycle.** This is a pyrido-oxazinone. The lactam ring has C(=O), then CH2, then O, then an aromatic carbon, then a second aromatic carbon bearing the lactam N. The pyridine ring is fused at those two carbons. The pyridine N is adjacent to the carbon attached to the lactam N.

Checking the pyridine ring: the N-bearing carbon (C8a) is bonded to the pyridine N, which is bonded to CH, CH, CH, and then the carbon bearing O. This gives c2cccnc2 with the O-carbon first and the N-carbon last, which matches the drawing.

**Piperidine.** The lactam N is attached to C4 of the piperidine, and the piperidine N carries the side chain.

**Linker.** From the piperidine N: CH2, CH(OH), CH2, then the pyrazole N1.

**Pyrazole core.** N1 is bonded to N2, and N2 is double-bonded to C3. C3 carries the 4-CF3-phenyl group. C3 is bonded to C3a, which is double-bonded to C7a, and C7a is bonded to N1. C3a connects to CH2 (C4), then N5 (bearing SO2Me), then CH2 (C6), then CH2 (C7), then back to C7a.

SMILES for this part: n1(CC(O)CN...)nc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)c2c1CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C2

The ring closure works out: c2 is C3a, then c1 is C7a closing to N1, then CCN is C7, C6, N5, and the final C2 is C4 closing to C3a.

**Full SMILES:**
O=C1COc2cccnc2N1C1CCN(CC(O)Cn2nc(-c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3)c3c2CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C3)CC1

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: O=C1COc2cccnc2N1C1CCN(CC(O)Cn2nc(-c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3)c3c2CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C3)CC1

name: rs_0124
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring with a benzyloxy group at C6 and an alanine methyl ester side chain at C3.

**Pyridine ring.** N is at the top left. Moving around the ring from N, one neighbour is the carbon bearing O (C2 in ring numbering) and the other is a CH. The CH–CH= carbon on the other side carries the CH2 side chain, which makes it C5 relative to the O-bearing carbon at C6. The ring is therefore a 2-benzyloxy-5-substituted pyridine.

**Side chain.** The ring carbon is attached to CH2, then to CH(NH2), then to CO2Me.

**Benzyloxy group.** The ring carbon bears O, which connects to CH2 and then to a phenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry.** The alpha carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

name: rs_0123
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring with the following substituents:
- C2 carries the carboxamide, C(=O)NH–Ar.
- C3 carries an acetoxy group, OC(C)=O.

The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin (oxindole) unit.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. The second ring is attached to it at the position meta to the acid. On the second ring, the carbon next to the biaryl bond bears OH, and the next carbon bears the NH–N= group. The OH and the hydrazine are therefore on adjacent carbons, and the ring is 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl relative to the biaryl bond.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with the NH on one side, and the geometry is ambiguous. In the picture, the HN is at lower left of the N=, and the C3 ring carbon sits below and to the right. The N= is at the top, with HN to its left and C3 below it. On C3, the substituent C2 (C=O) points to the lower left and C3a points to the right. The NH is on the left of the N, and the C2 carbonyl side is on the left of C3, so these are on the same side (Z). SMILES written as: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(cc3)C(F)(F)F)c3ccccc23)c1O

Checking the geometry: in `N/N=C2/C(=O)...`, the N before the first bond is written "N/N", meaning the aryl-NH is below the N=. Then `=C2/C(=O)` places C(=O) above C. These are opposite sides of the double bond, which would make the NH and C2 trans (E). To get Z, I use `N/N=C2\C(=O)`.

name: rs_0251
text:
I read the structure in four parts and then joined them.

- **Indazole:** a 1H-indazole whose 6-position carries a C(=O) group. That carbonyl is bonded to the ring nitrogen of the tetrahydroisoquinoline.
- **Tetrahydroisoquinoline:** the ring nitrogen is acylated by the indazole carbonyl. On the aromatic ring, C5 and C7 carry Cl, and C6 carries the carboxamide C(=O)NH.
- **Amino acid unit:** the amide NH is attached to an alpha carbon bearing CO2H and a CH2NH side chain, which is a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit. The CH2 bond is drawn as a wedge. Ranking the substituents as N > CO2H > CH2 > H places the centre at S, the L configuration. I wrote it as `N[C@@H](CN...)C(=O)O`, which gives S by analogy with L-serine, since CH2N ranks the same as CH2OH there.
- **Cyanoguanidine and cyclobutane:** the side-chain NH is bonded to C(=N–C≡N)–NH. That NH is bonded to a cyclobutane carrying NMe2 on the carbon opposite (1,3-position). The cyclobutane bonds are plain, so I gave no cis/trans stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN(C)C1CC(C1)NC(=NC#N)NC[C@H](NC(=O)c1c(Cl)cc2CN(CCc2c1Cl)C(=O)c1ccc2cn[nH]c2c1)C(=O)O

I wrote the final string with the alpha carbon as `[C@H]` after the side-chain CH2, a different atom order from the fragment above. I did not re-derive the chirality tag for this order; the check was done on the `N[C@@H](CN...)C(=O)O` form, so the tag in the final string may need confirming.

name: rs_0254
text:
I read the molecule as a 6,7-dihydro-5H-pyrrolo[1,2-a]imidazole core with these substituents:

- **Imidazole carbons:** one carries the 4-fluorophenyl group and the other carries a pyridin-4-yl group. The pyridine has an NH-cyclobutyl group at its 2-position.
- **Bridgehead nitrogen:** it is attached to the saturated ring carbon, which bears a CH2–O–CH2–(4-methoxyphenyl) side chain.
- **Ring fusion:** the C=N carbon of the imidazole is bonded to a CH2–CH2 unit that closes the five-membered ring onto that stereocentre.

**Stereochemistry:** only the ring carbon carrying the CH2O substituent is marked, with a hashed bond to the CH2O group, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.

- CIP priorities at that carbon are N (bridgehead), then CH2O, then the ring CH2.
- On the page, N → CH2O → ring CH2 runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, that reverses to clockwise, giving R.
- In the SMILES below, `[C@H]` with neighbour order (ring CH2, H, CH2O, N) also works out to R, so it matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccc(COC[C@H]2CCc3nc(-c4ccc(F)cc4)c(-c4ccnc(NC5CCC5)c4)n32)cc1

I rewrote the SMILES from the check above so the stereo tag matches the neighbour order. In this written form the chiral atom is preceded by the CH2O carbon, so I re-derived the tag as follows. The neighbours in order are CH2O, H, ring CH2, N. Swapping to put H first gives (H, CH2O, C6, N) with one swap, so the sense flips relative to the tag. For `@` the order CH2O, H, C6, N becomes `@@` with H first, meaning CH2O → C6 → N is clockwise from H. Seen from the side opposite H, this is counterclockwise, which is equivalent to N → CH2O → C6 counterclockwise, i.e. S. So `@` here gives S, and R needs `@@`.

Corrected:

SMILES: COc1ccc(COC[C@@H]2CCc3nc(-c4ccc(F)cc4)c(-c4ccnc(NC5CCC5)c4)n32)cc1

name: rs_0247
text:
I read the molecule region by region and assembled the SMILES below. I derived the stereochemistry by hand from the wedges and hashes, using CIP priorities, and did not run it through a toolkit.

**Fragments**
- **Indazole:** a 1H-indazole attached through C6 (the benzo-ring carbon bearing the carbonyl) to a C(=O) group.
- **Tetrahydroisoquinoline:** that carbonyl acylates the ring nitrogen N2. The ring carries Cl at C5 and C7, and a carboxamide at C6.
- **Amino acid chain:** the carboxamide NH is attached to a CH(CO2H)–CH2–NH unit.
- **Cyanoguanidine:** the terminal NH is bonded to a C(=N–C≡N) carbon, which is also bonded to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** a 3,5-dihydroxypiperidine ring.

**Stereocentres**
- **Alpha carbon:** the wedge goes to the CH2. With the implicit H pointing away, N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S.
- **Piperidine C3:** the OH is hashed, so it is R.
- **Piperidine C5:** the OH is wedged, so it is R.
- The two ring hydroxyls are therefore trans, (3R,5R).

name: rs_0256
text:

**Biphenyl part:** The top-left ring carries CO2H. A second ring is attached to it at the position meta to the CO2H. On that second ring, the carbon bearing the first ring is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon bears the NH–N= group.

**Hydrazone and indolinone:** The NH is bonded to N=, which is double-bonded to C3 of the indolin-2-one. C2 is C=O and N1 carries a 4-propylphenyl group. The CF3 sits on the benzo ring at position 5, which is para to N1. C3a is bonded to C3, and C4 is the CH next to C3a. Going around the ring, C5 is the next carbon and carries the CF3.

**Propyl chain:** From the phenyl ring the chain runs CH2–CH2–CH2, which is three carbons, so the group is propyl. The drawing shows the ring carbon, then a bond down-left, then a bond down, then a bond down-right, giving three carbons.

**Stereochemistry:** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits on the upper left of N, and N is attached to C3 of the indolinone. At C3 the substituents are C2 (the carbonyl, lower left) and C3a (right). The N= is at about (297, 400) with NH at (215, 380) to its left. C3 is at (320, 455), below and to the right of N. Looking at the C=N bond, the NH on N points left. On C3, C2 points left-down and C3a points right. The NH therefore lies on the same side as C2 (the left side), which makes it Z with respect to the carbonyl side.

For the SMILES, I write `N(/N=C1/C(=O)...)` with the matching bond marks. Using the form `Oc1c(...)cccc1N/N=C1\C(=O)N(Ar)c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc12`: the N before the bond is written as `N/N=C1\C(=O)`. This means the NH is on the "below" side of the first bond and C(=O) is on the "below" side of the second bond with the backslash, which puts them on the same side (cis).

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(CCC)cc3)c3ccc(cc23)C(F)(F)F)c1O

name: rs_0257
text:

On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the C–OH carbon, and the C–OH carbon is adjacent to the carbon bearing NH. So the OH sits between the aryl group and the hydrazine NH.

**Hydrazone linker.** The NH is joined to N by a double bond, and that N is attached to C3 of the indolinone.

**Indolinone part.** C3 is double-bonded to the hydrazone N. C2 is C=O and is bonded to N1. N1 carries a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group and is also fused to the benzo ring.

- Second ring: c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c4)c5ccccc35)c2O

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn without explicit cis/trans geometry that I can assign with confidence, so I left it unspecified.

name: rs_0259
text:

- **Benzoic acid end:** a para-substituted benzene bearing COOH, with a CH2 attached at the para position.
- **Linker:** the CH2 connects to an N that carries a methyl group. That N is bonded to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** N is on C1, a methyl is on C2 (ortho to N), and the ether O is on C4 (para to N). The ring runs C1(N), C2(CH3), C3(H), C4(O), C5(H), C6(H).

  - C5 is bonded to O1, and O1 is bonded to N2, which is double-bonded to C3.

name: rs_0258
text:

The ring size is inferred from that geometry rather than seen in full.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are no wedges or hashes, and the quaternary carbon is not a stereocentre because its ring is symmetric. No stereo marks are needed.

text:

name: rs_0261
text:
The drawing shows an acrylic acid attached to a hydroxyphenyl hydrazone of an N-aryl isatin. I read it region by region.

**Acrylic acid chain.** CO2H sits on a carbon that also carries a methyl group. That carbon is double-bonded to a CH, which connects to the benzene ring. This gives HOOC–C(CH3)=CH–Ar.

The drawing shows the CH= on the left and the CO2H on top of the carbon bearing Me. The ring is attached at the lower left of the double bond, and the CO2H goes up from the right carbon. Methyl is to the right and down. On the left carbon (CH), the substituents are the ring (down) and H. On the right carbon, the substituents are CO2H (up) and Me (right-down). The ring and CO2H are therefore on opposite sides of the double bond (ring below-left, CO2H above), which is trans, so the aryl and COOH are E. In SMILES: OC(=O)/C(C)=C/Ar, where the COOH and the Ar are on opposite sides.

**Central benzene ring.** The ring carbon attached to the alkene is C1. Going around the ring, the next carbon (upper left) is CH, then C–OH (left), then C–NH (bottom), then CH, then CH. The OH carbon is meta to the alkene and the NH carbon is para to it.

**Hydrazone and oxindole.** The NH–N= unit connects to C3 of the oxindole. C3 is bonded to C2 (C=O), and C2 is bonded to N1, which carries the 3,5-dimethylphenyl group. The benzo ring bears CF3. Going round the benzo ring from C3a, the carbons are C4, C5, C6 (bearing CF3), C7, and C7a, which is bonded to N. The CF3 is drawn on the carbon that is para to C3a, which is C6.

The hydrazone C=N geometry is not clearly drawn as a defined stereo bond, so I leave it unspecified.

SMILES: OC(=O)/C(C)=C/c1ccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3cc(C)cc(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc23)c(O)c1

name: rs_0262
text:

- **Position 7:** Cl.
- **Position 6:** methyl.
- **Position 3:** a CH2C(=O)NH-aryl group. The aryl ring is 4-fluoro-2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl: the N-bearing carbon is C1, CF3 is at C2 and F is at C4.
- **Position 4:** a phenyl ring that is meta-substituted with CH2-NH-CH2-CO2Et.

- C5 is followed by C6 (methyl), then C7 (Cl), then C8-H, then C8a, which bonds to O1.

Amide aryl group: N-c1ccc(F)cc1C(F)(F)F

- c1 is the N-bearing carbon, followed by c (H), c (H), c(F), c (H), and finally c1 bearing CF3.
- In the picture, the N-bearing carbon is at the lower left of the ring, CF3 is below it, and F is at the top right, which matches 4-fluoro-2-CF3.

Check on the ring closure in the last fragment: C1=C(...)C(=O)Oc2cc(Cl)c(C)cc12. The aromatic atoms are c2 (C8a), c (C8), c(Cl) (C7), c(C) (C6), c (C5) and c12 (C4a). C4a closes ring 1 to C4 and ring 2 to C8a, so the ring system is correct.

name: rs_0263
text:

name: rs_0264
text:
I read the structure as a 2-benzoxazolone core (a fused benzene and oxazolone ring) with three substituents:

- **Ring system:** the oxazolone ring has O at the top, a C=O carbon, and an NH at the bottom. It is fused to the benzene ring.

For the SMILES `COC(=O)[C@H](N)Cc1cc(Br)c2[nH]c(=O)oc2c1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CO2Me, H, N, CH2. The `@` label for this order corresponds to R, which matches the drawing.

name: rs_0255
text:
I read the drawing as a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypyridine-2-carboxamide whose amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl-substituted norbornane. I could not tell from the image which way the bridging carbon sits in depth, so the bridgehead stereo rests on the usual perspective reading; the two wedge-defined centres do not depend on it.

**Pyridine ring and amide**
- The pyridine ring has an OMe at C4 and an OH at C3.
- C2 carries C(=O)NH, and N is the ring nitrogen at the bottom left.

**Norbornane (bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane)**
- The two bridgehead carbons are joined by a one-carbon bridge at the top.
- The amide NH is on a carbon next to one bridgehead, on the left two-carbon bridge. The bond is a wedge.
- The phenyl is on a carbon next to the same bridgehead, on the right two-carbon bridge. The bond is also a wedge.

**Stereochemistry**
- The two wedged carbons (C–N and C–Ph) were assigned directly from the 2D wedge geometry.
- The two bridgeheads have no wedges, so I assigned them from a 3D reading of the perspective drawing. I took the upper bridgehead as the rear one and the lower bridgehead as the front one, with the one-carbon bridge on top.

The SMILES below was checked by hand against the ring closures and chirality ordering.

name: rs_0268

name: rs_0265
text:
I read the structure in three parts and then assigned the two stereocentres from the wedges.

**Pyridine ring:** The ring nitrogen is adjacent to C2, which carries the carboxamide C(=O)NH. C3 carries OH, C4 carries OMe, and C5 and C6 are CH.

**Cyclohexane ring:** The ring has six carbons.
- C1 is quaternary. It bears a methyl and a C(=O)N(CH3)CH2CH2Ph group (an N‑methyl‑N‑phenethyl amide).
- C2 is CH2.
- C3 is CH and bears the NH of the pyridine amide.
- C4 is CH2.
- C5 is a gem‑dimethyl carbon.
- C6 is CH2.

- At C1, the priorities are C(=O)N > C2 > C6 > CH3. C2 outranks C6 because C2 leads to C3, which carries N. The triple-product test on the drawn geometry gives S. This corresponds to `[C@@]` in my SMILES order.

text:

name: rs_0269

name: rs_0274
text:
The drawing shows an isatin hydrazone: an oxindole (indol-2-one) with a hydrazone at C3, an N1-aryl group and a CF3 on the benzo ring.

**Acrylic acid part.** CO2H is attached to a carbon bearing Me, which is double-bonded to a CH that connects to the aryl ring. This gives HOOC-C(Me)=CH-Ar. The drawing places the aryl (lower left) and the CO2H (up) on the same side of the double bond. The Me points right and the CH's aryl points down-left. On the CH carbon, the substituent Ar goes down, and on the other carbon, CO2H goes up and Me goes right. Ar is down and CO2H is up, so they are on opposite sides, which makes Ar and CO2H trans (E). The double bond is drawn with the CH at the left (about x=147, y=113) and C at (205, 75). From C, CO2H goes up and Me goes lower right. From CH, Ar goes down. The substituents are CO2H (up) on C and Ar (down) on CH, so they are trans.

**Central phenyl ring.** The attachments are the acrylic chain, OH and NHN. The chain carbon is at the top, OH is on the adjacent meta position, and the NH is para to the chain carbon, ortho to OH.

**Oxindole.** C3(=N-NH-Ar) is attached to C3a. C2 is C=O and is bonded to N1, which carries the 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. CF3 is on the benzo carbon that is para to C3a, i.e. position 6. The ring runs C3a, C4, C5, C6(CF3), C7, C7a. In the drawing, C7a bonds to N, and C7 is the lower carbon, which is attached to the carbon bearing CF3. This gives position 6.

**Hydrazone geometry.** This is not specified clearly, so I leave it unspecified.

**SMILES** (with E on the alkene):
C/C(C(=O)O)=C\c1ccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc32)c(O)c1

Checking the alkene notation: C/C(C(=O)O)=C\c1... has Me "/" before C, and the aryl "\" after the =C. Me is below the double bond going up, as in F/C=C\F, which is cis for Me and Ar. So Me and Ar are cis, and CO2H and Ar are trans, as required.

SMILES: C/C(C(=O)O)=C\c1ccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc32)c(O)c1

name: rs_0277
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

OC(=O)CC1CCc2c1[nH]c1ccc(F)cc21

name: rs_0295
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. The second ring is attached to it at the position meta to the CO2H. That second ring has OH ortho to the biaryl bond, and an NH–N= group on the carbon next to the OH carbon. This makes it a 3'-hydrazinyl-2'-hydroxybiphenyl-3-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone part.** NH–N= connects to C3 of the oxindole. C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. In the fused benzene ring, C3a is attached to C3 and C4 bears the methyl. C5 bears F, then C6 and C7 are CH, and C7a is attached to N1.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows the C=N double bond with the NH on one side and the C=O on the other. I'll write it with explicit geometry.

In the image, the N= sits above C3 and the NH lies to the left and below it. The ring carbon C3 has C2 (the carbonyl, to the lower left) and C3a (to the right). The N= is bonded up and slightly left of C3, and NH is down-left of the N. So NH is on the same side as C2 (the carbonyl side), giving a Z arrangement.

SMILES for the double bond: C3(=N/N...) written as O=C1N(Ar)c2ccc(F)c(C)c2/C1=N/Nc...

For this fragment, C1 is the carbon with neighbors C(=O) (written before it) and c2 (written as the preceding atom in the ring). I'll write it as `C1(=N\N...)`, where the preceding atom is c2 (C3a). To place NH on the C2 side, which is opposite to C3a, I use:

c2/C1=N/N

Here c2 is "below" the bond (/ before C1) and N/N is "above" it, so they are trans. That puts NH trans to C3a and therefore cis to C2, as required.

Full SMILES:
OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(F)c(C)c23)c1O

Checking the stereo in this form: the atom before the double bond is N (via "/N="), and after C2 comes "/C(=O)", so the NH and the C=O are trans. That is the opposite of what I want, so I flip it to N\N=C2/C(=O)...

Here N\N=C2/C(=O): the first N (the NH) has the bond "\" written before the second N, and C(=O) has "/" after C2. That gives NH and C=O cis, which is the Z arrangement I want.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N\N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(F)c(C)c23)c1O

The drawing shows a 4-substituted benzoic acid joined through a two-carbon chain to the nitrogen of a pyrrolidin-2-one. The lactam ring carbon next to nitrogen carries a 3-hydroxynonyl chain.

**Stereochemistry**
- Lactam ring carbon (wedge to the chain): the CIP priorities are N, then ring CH2, then the chain CH2, then H. The ring CH2 outranks the chain CH2 because its path reaches the C=O carbon (O,O,N) sooner. With H pointing back, N → ring CH2 → chain runs counterclockwise, so this centre is S. In the SMILES this is `[C@H]`.
- Carbinol carbon (hashed OH): the priorities are OH, then the chain branch toward the ring, then the chain branch toward the terminal CH3, then H. With OH hashed and H toward the viewer, the sense of the OH → ring-side → CH3-side sequence is reversed, so this centre is also S. In the SMILES this is `[C@@H]`.

name: rs_0326
text:
The structure is a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. Its meta position links to the second ring. On the second ring, the carbon next to the biaryl bond bears OH, and the next carbon bears NH–N=.

**Oxindole part.**
- C3 is double-bonded to N (the hydrazone).
- C2 is C=O.
- N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group.
- The benzo ring carries OCF3. Numbering from the N-attached ring carbon C7a, the ring goes C7a, C7 (CH), C6 (the carbon bearing OCF3), C5, C4, C3a. In the drawing, the carbon bearing OCF3 is attached to the CH adjacent to C7a, so OCF3 is at C6.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows the C=N double bond with the NH on one side. Reading the coordinates: N= sits at (285, 410) and is bonded to NH at (230, 380) to its upper left. C3 is at (285, 485), directly below. At C3, the substituents are C2 (carbonyl, lower left, at 250, 530) and C3a (right, at 340, 485). The NH on the N is to the left, on the same side as C2, so the NH and C2 are cis (Z).

**SMILES.**
- Ring part: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(OC(F)(F)F)ccc23)c1O
- Writing the stereo as N/N=C2/...: the fragment is c(N/N=C2\C(=O)N...)…
- For the Z form, NH and C2 are on the same side. I write `N/N=C2/C(=O)...`. With the F/C=C/F pattern, the two substituents are trans. The N is written before the double bond with "/", and C(=O) follows the C2 atom with "/", which gives trans, so NH and C=O would be trans. To get cis, I use `\` after C2: `N/N=C2\C(=O)N(...)c3cc(...)ccc23`.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(OC(F)(F)F)ccc23)c1O

name: rs_0324
